exceptions.rationale: Existing infallible signatures retain documented preconditions and may panic or yield nonfinite signals on invalid direct Rust input. Changing signatures would break embedding clients; checked alternatives bound external paths.
exceptions.mitigations: Use checked constructors/arithmetic/queries/minimizer/swaption for external input. FFI applies resource/domain validation. Nonfinite minimizer/pricer failure cannot be treated as successful economics. Core compatibility conversion accepts declared period counts only. Pure callbacks must terminate and not panic. Existing signatures are not certified total APIs.

exceptions.rationale: Legacy infallible calendar/day-count search APIs rely on ordered representable dates, valid periods and calendars with reachable business days. Existing file-loading convenience methods remain; a universal checked schedule API is separate scope.
exceptions.mitigations: Host dates are years 1..9999 and instrument spans at most 150*366 days, using built-in calendars. Do not pass pathological custom calendars or boundary dates to unchecked search APIs. Checked date offset regression/property tests run. File conveniences are setup only and never provider/runtime dependencies of pricing. Complete checked shared primitives and move side-effect conveniences at the owning task.

exceptions.rationale: Existing monotone-convex has a nonnegative-forward model constraint; UFR is heuristic; SequentialBootstrapper is an approximate quote-curve diagnostic whose historical completion flag reports construction. No new model convention or standalone product completeness is certified.
exceptions.mitigations: Keep negative-rate support in other suitable interpolators without banning discount factors >1. Use checked global/piecewise fitting for production ingress; verify requested residuals and propagate failures. Do not present SequentialBootstrapper completion as repricing convergence or use the heuristic as Smith-Wilson. Independent curve/model certification remains required.

exceptions.rationale: Existing orchestration/dispatch algorithms exceed a one-screen function guideline. Selected measured spans before next format: LM lines 355..467 (113 source lines); scenario_inner 1084..1188 (105 source lines). Splitting branch/state logic only to meet line counts can hide invariants.
exceptions.mitigations: Hash-pin the critical sources, keep input bounds at ingress, test helper error/repricing, generation fencing and concurrent claims, and require focused complexity/state-transition review when changed. Pure scope lints remain active. This exception does not suppress compiler warnings or authorize new unbounded numerical work. Existing runtime graph sizes/queues/timeouts are explicit; distributed/steady-state allocation certification is separate.
